title: Thermodynamic Systems, Surroundings And Boundaries
description: A draft foundation lesson for selecting and classifying thermodynamic systems before equations or property data are introduced.
learningOutcomes: Identify a selected thermodynamic system, its surroundings, and its boundary.
Distinguish closed, open, and isolated system classifications from stated boundary conditions.
Distinguish property, state, process, cycle, intensive property, and extensive property vocabulary.

blocks.text: This draft lesson introduces the vocabulary needed to declare a thermodynamic system and boundary before later analysis begins.
Students need only basic physical-science vocabulary; this lesson introduces no thermodynamic equation or property table.
After the lesson, students should be able to declare a system and boundary, classify what may cross that boundary, and use introductory property and process vocabulary consistently.
A thermodynamic explanation is ambiguous until the selected system and boundary are stated, because that selection determines how mass and energy interactions will be described in later lessons.

blocks.definition: The system is the matter or region selected for analysis, the surroundings are everything outside it, and the boundary separates the two.
A closed system contains a fixed quantity of matter, an open system allows mass to cross its selected boundary, and an isolated system exchanges neither matter nor energy with its surroundings.
Properties describe a system state; a process changes the state; a cycle returns the system to its initial state after a sequence of processes.
An intensive property does not depend on the amount of matter selected, while an extensive property does.

blocks.title: Selected system and boundary
blocks.altText: A labelled boundary encloses the selected system, with surroundings outside and arrows indicating that possible crossings depend on the chosen classification.
blocks.description: The boundary is drawn around the selected matter or region. The classification question is whether matter or energy may cross that boundary.
blocks.caption: Original Industrial Learn concept diagram; no source figure is reproduced.

blocks.text: System classification follows the selected boundary. A closed-system analysis follows a fixed quantity of matter, while an open-system analysis uses a control volume that mass may cross.
A sealed system is not automatically isolated: isolation also requires that energy not be exchanged with the surroundings.
Each exercise states one selected boundary and asks only for classification; no unprovided property value or equipment limit may be inferred.
No equation is required for this classification lesson. Energy balances, property relations, and process equations belong to later source-reviewed lessons.

blocks.title: Classify a sealed classroom container
given: The sealed contents are selected as the system.
The container wall is selected as the boundary.

steps.label: Declare the system
steps.explanation: The selected matter is stated explicitly.

steps.label: Declare the surroundings
steps.explanation: The wall separates the selected system from its surroundings.

steps.label: Classify mass crossing
steps.expression: mass crossing = none for the stated sealed case
steps.explanation: The selected matter is treated as a closed system for this exercise.

blocks.result: Closed system for the stated classroom classification.
blocks.interpretation: The classification does not imply isolation, operating limits, or permission to use real equipment.

blocks.text: Internal review-gated activity: select whether mass and energy may cross one stated boundary, then inspect the resulting open, closed, isolated, or indeterminate classification. The activity remains unavailable for student attempts until independent review is recorded.

blocks.title: Changing the boundary during an explanation
symptoms: The answer alternates between the contents and the entire device as the system.
The learner cannot state whether mass crosses the selected boundary.
likelyCauses: The system and boundary were not declared first.
blocks.safeResponse: Stop, restate the selected system and boundary, and repeat the classification without changing them.

blocks.title: Classification is not operating authority
blocks.text: This lesson does not establish pressure limits, temperature limits, equipment ratings, or permission to open, heat, pressurise, or operate real equipment.

blocks.prompt: Which classification describes a selected region whose boundary may be crossed by mass?
blocks.answerExplanation: An open system is represented by a control volume whose selected boundary may be crossed by mass.

blocks.text: Start thermodynamic analysis by declaring the system, surroundings, and boundary. Classify the system from what may cross that boundary, then use property, state, process, and cycle vocabulary without inventing property data.

blocks.note: Purdue ME 20000 Lecture 1, pages 6 to 7, supports the system, boundary, classification, property, state, process, and intensive/extensive definitions used in this draft.
OpenStax College Physics, section 15.2, supports the cycle definition used in this draft.
